            At present, Board of SIDBI Pension Fund Trust includes one SIDBI Board member, one representative each from
officers, Class III and Class IV, retired employees. Chairman of SIDBI becomes Ex-officio Chairman of Pension Trust.
 
            Since, the Pension Trust belongs to SIDBI and is widely represented, the need for associating a Government
representative in the Board of Trustees has not been felt.
 
            Committee's Observation (27.04.04):-
 
            The Committee was not satisfied with the Ministry's comments and desired that representatives of Government and
Trade Unions should be provided a place in Board of Trustees.
 
            Action Taken by the Ministry (27.07.04):-
      
 
Adopted from IDBI.
 
            The variation in the number of trustees is to take care of the minimum working requirement on one hand and future
expansion in case of substantial increase in the staff of the Bank requiring broad basing of the trustees, on the other.
 
            The guidelines regarding appointment of trustees, their duties and responsibilities, vacation of post etc. are given in the
Deed of Trust.
 
            At present, Board of SIDBI Pension Fund Trust comprises five officers and one Class III – Class IV representative from
SIDBI – Executive Director in charge of Administration is the Chairman while the Chief General Manager of PF-Pension Cell is
the Alternative Chairman.
 
            As the Pension Trust pertains to SIDBI, which has adequate representation, the need is not felt to provide for
Government representation. 
 
            Committee’s further Observation (22.02.05):-
 
            The Committee was not satisfied with the Ministry’s comments for not including representatives of Government and the
Trade Unions in the Board of Trustees. The Committee reiterated its earlier stand that the representatives of Government and the
Trade Unions should be included in the Board of Trustees.

            The constitution of the SIDBI Trust has been laid down in Regulation No. 9 of the SIDB Pension Regulations. As per the
Regulations, the composition of the Board shall not be less than three and not more than nine. This regulation is similar to the
regulations adopted by the other DFIs and nationalized banks. Further, the Pension Trust is represented by different groups
including representatives of Class III and Class IV employees apart from other members. Regarding representative from the
Government of India in the Board of Trustees, the Government may take a view in the matter.
 
8)         Point Raised:-
 
            Regulation 15: "Pension subject to future good conduct"
 
            In regulation 15, pension or a part thereof may be withheld or withdrawn if a pensioner is convicted of a serious crime or
is found guilty of grave misconduct. The terms 'serious crime' and 'grave misconduct' are capable of assuming varied
interpretations. Whether Government have any objection in making the provisions of regulation 15 specific?
 
            Ministry's Reply (01.07.03)
 
            It would not be possible to comprehend all types of serious crimes or grave misconduct which could necessitate
withholding or withdrawing pension or a part thereof whether permanently or for a specified period. In the CCS Pension Rules
applicable to the Central Government employees, similar provisions have been incorporated without defining the terms 'serious
crime" and "grave misconduct".
 
Committee's Observation (27.04.04)
 
            The Committee noted the Ministry's comments.
 
9)         Point Raised:-
 
Regulation 39:- Commutation
 
            "A pensioner may commute for a lump-sum payment, a fraction upto maximum of one-third of the pension admissible to
him. Such a pensioner will be entitled to the pension upto two-third portion of the admissible pension. Commuted portion of the
pension will be resorted after a period of fifteen years from the date of commutation. The method of commutation shall be in
accordance with the table enclosed hereto. If commutation is sought after one year of the ate of retirement, it will be granted
only after medical examination, by the Medical Officer of the Small Industries Bank."
 
            Under the provisions of this regulation, a pensioner may commute one-third of the admissible pension while under the
CCS (Pension) Rules, a pensioner may commute up to 40% of admissible pension. Whether Government have any objection in
maintaining parity in this regard?
 
            Ministry's Reply (01.07.03):-
 
            The subject regulation is exactly in line with similar such regulations applicable in IDBI and RBI. As SIDBI shares the
same parentage and as and when any revision in the Regulations of RBI and IDBI takes place, SIDBI will consider the same
principles for adoption.
 
            Committee's Observation (27.04.04):-
 
            The Committee was informed that the provision is exactly in line with the similar provision in IDBI and RBI Regulation.
The Committee desired the Ministry to review the relevant provisions of SIDBI, RBI and IDBI.
 
Action Taken by the Ministry (10.06.04):-
 
            The subject regulation has been adopted from IDBI. However, it is understood that RBI has made a reference to GoI for
increase in the commutation percentage to 40%. We propose to initiate necessary steps for the same.
 
10)       Point Raised:-
 
            There is a discrepancy in the numbering of the regulations. For example, in regulation 1 and 3, the sub-regulations have
been numbered as (i), (ii) etc. whereas in regulations 2, 6 and 9, these have been numbered as (1), (2), (3) etc. Further, in
regulation 8, the sub-regulations have been numbered as (a), (b), (c) etc. an so on. Whether the ministry has any objection in

correcting the number of the sub-regulations and providing uniformity in this regard?
 
            Ministry's Reply (01.07.03):-
 
            The suggestions of the Committee are accepted.
 
            Committee's Observation (27.04.04):-
 
            The Ministry agreed to the Committee's suggestion to rectify the position.
 
            Action Taken by the Ministry:-
 
            We propose to make necessary changes for the sake of uniformity together with the other proposed amendments to the
regulations.
 
3.         The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Finance had accepted its suggestions as under:-
 
(i)
                  In Regulation 9, by indicating the different groups including representatives of Class III and Class IV employees,
and an Officer of the rank of Under Secretary from the Ministry of Finance  apart from other members that can be or
should be included in the Board of Trustees of the Bank. The Committee had impressed upon the Government to
indicate the category of persons that can or should be included in the Board of Trustees.
 
(ii)
                In Regulation 39, by proposing to initiate necessary steps to increase the commutation percentage in case of
pensioners to 40% of admissible pension. The Committee had pointed out that under the provisions of the present
Regulations, a pensioner may commute one third of the admissible pension while under the CCS (Pension) Rules, a
pensioner may commute up to 40% of admissible pension. It had suggested to the Government to maintain parity in
this regard.
 
(iii)               On the issue raised vide point no 10, by proposing to make necessary changes in the numbering of the regulations.
The Committee had pointed out the discrepancy in the numbering of the regulations and had suggested correction
therein for the sake of uniformity.
 
4.         The Committee is, however, unhappy to note the shift in the Ministry’s stand from time to time while corresponding
with it on various points in the questionnaire; like point nos. 1, 2, 3, and 6, to mention a few. While the Committee agrees to
some extent to the Government’s logic to keep in line with the Pension Regulations of other financial institutions, but in that
case they should not act as an obstacle and retard the evolution in similar legislation that is taking place in other
institutions/organizations of Government.   For example, inclusion of part time workers within the definition of the term
‘employee’, Regulation 2(7) does not go well with the present time.   In Committee’s view, SIDBI is a statutory body and it
should have an effective and efficient set of subordinate legislations to enable it to discharge its obligations responsibly, and it
should not feel constrained on any account, including the keeping of parity with other financial institutions, in this endeavour of
theirs.  The Committee, accordingly, recommends the Ministry to review the regulations in the light of the Committee
suggestions that have been put forth during the course of its deliberations, keeping aside all constraints that have been pointed
out so that Regulations are efficient and relevant to the current times.
SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS
           
The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Finance (Banking Division) have accepted most of its recommendations
and has taken necessary action upon them as under:
·        Rule2 (d):    By agreeing to add the words “to mean a person registered as a valuer under Section 34 AB of Wealth Tax Act, 1957
and approved by the Board of Directors or Board of Trustees of the secured creditor, as the case may be”, and there by specifying the
qualifications of the 'Approved Valuer'.
·        Rule8 (2):   By agreeing to add the words " as soon as possible but in any case not later than 7 days from the date of taking
possession", thereby specifying the time period for publishing the possession notice after the taking over of the property.
·
        Rule9 (7):   By agreeing to add the following provisio below the rule in order to check the misuse of the excess money:
“Provided that if after meeting the cost of removing encumbrances and contingencies there is any surplus available out of the
money deposited by the purchaser such surplus shall be paid to the purchaser within 15 days from the date of finalisation of the sale”.
·
        Rule9 (8):      By agreeing to substitute the word "shall" with "may", so as to make it obligatory for the authorised officer or
purchaser to issue notices to the interested or entitled persons.
·
        Rule10 (1):    By agreeing to add the following proviso in order to specify the qualifications of the 'Manager' :
“Provided that the Manager so appointed shall not be a person who is, or at any time has been, adjudicated insolvent, or has
suspended payment or has compounded with his creditors, or who is, or has been convicted by a criminal Court of an offence

involving moral turpitude”.
 
On the rest of the points, the Committee noted the explanation furnished by the Ministry.
 
The Committee, however, recommends that the Ministry of Finance (Banking Division) should carry out the
modifications in the Rules agreed to by them as above, at the earliest.
 
II
 
The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Law & Justice (Department of Legal Affairs) have reached
favourably on the various points that were referred to them for comments/clarifications. The Committee notes that the Ministry
have agreed to take action as follows in pursuance to its suggestions:

  To provide that the Chairperson presiding over the meeting, exercises his voting right only in cases
where there is a tie in the votes cast, for the purpose of resolution of the same.
            Point 3 (Rule 12(1)):
 (i) To provide a specific time period of 4 months for issuing a certificate for recognition in Form-
IV.
            (ii) To provide for an authority for appeal/ review if the application for recognition is rejected which may be the State
Bar Council of each State.
           
Point 5 (Rule 14):
  (i) To prescribe 6 months as the period for seeking re-admission as a member of the fund and by
fixing the interest on arrears at the time of re-admission at not exceeding 3%.
            (ii) To prescribe a period of 15 days to ensure continuity of the membership of the fund and that the membership may be
discontinued if the member failed to respond.
            Point 6 (Rule 15
):  To prescribe 6 months period for the issuance of certificate of membership to the fund.
            Point 7 (Rule 16): To increase the period from 15 to 45 days for intimating the removal/ suspension of a member from
the State roll to the Trustee Committee.
            Point 8 (Rule 19): 
To substitute the word 'thiery' with the word 'thirty', thereby rectifying a typographical error.
 
On rest of the points the Committee notes with satisfaction the explanation furnished by the Ministry.
 
            The Committee, however recommends that the Ministry of Law and Justice should carry out modification in the Rules as
agreed to by them, expeditiously.
 
III
            The Committee notes with satisfaction that IRDA have taken a decision to implement the Government orders on
reservations for the reserved category persons and allow to them suitable relaxation in age, educational qualification,
experience, etc. The Committee recommends that the policy decision of IRDA should find a clear mention in their Regulation,
so that the policy gets a statutory recognition. As regard to the autonomy conferred upon IRDA in the matter of recruitment and
promotion, the Committee feel that the justification given for the autonomy may no doubt sound appealing, but vesting of wide 
discretion  in any authority is always liable to be misused.
 
While the Committee appreciates the need for autonomy as projected by the IRDA, but in the Committee’s view,
subordinate legislation in the form of Rules/ Regulations should be codified to the optimum, particularly when they to regulate
the recruitment/promotion policy of an organization which has a bearing on its manpower. Accordingly, the Committee
recommends that IRDA may review their regulations to see to what extent they can do away with the element of subjectivity, of
course without compromising with their efficiency standards.

class of cargo at a time.

behalf, do hereby present this Hundred and Seventieth Report of the Committee.
.
1.2       The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on  29th August, 2007.
 
1.3       The notifications containing Rules/Regulations, etc. which were laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha during its 210 th Session
(February- March, April-May, 2007) have been perused by the Committee in the light of the provisions of the Acts under which these
were framed and also with a view to see whether these have been laid properly and within the prescribed time-frame.   The Committee’s
observations/recommendations are contained in the report that follows.
 
NEW DELHI
29th August, 2007
 
 
DR. (SHRIMATI) NAJMA A. HEPTULLA
Chairperson
Committee on Subordinate Legislation,
Rajya Sabha
                                                            
 
 
Report

        Laying of Statutory Orders on the Table of Rajya Sabha

th  Session of the Rajya Sabha,     (23rd February to 21st March, 23rd April to 17th May,  2007) 186 Statutory Orders
relating to Rules/Regulations/Schemes/Bye-laws framed under the Constitution/ Acts of Parliament were laid on the Table of the House
by various Ministries/Departments. The details of the Gazette Notifications in which these were published, the date of their laying on the
Table of the Rajya Sabha have been indicated in the Ministry-wise statement placed at Annexure. Out of the above notifications that were
laid, there has been delay in laying of some of the notifications as per the details given below: -

2.         During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has noted some cases where there has been a considerable time lag
between the date of notification of the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also indicates the period of delay in cases
where notifications have not been laid as per the schedule prescribed by the Committee and where such notifications were accompanied
by a statement indicating the reasons for the delay in laying. In some of the cases the delay has been quite long. The
observations/recommendations of the Committee in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments are as follows: -  
           
(i) Ministry of Civil Aviation
 
            The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of up to eleven months on the part of the Ministry of Civil Aviation in
laying three of their notifications (Sl. Nos 2,3,& 4) and  in all the cases the Ministry have not appended the delay statements .
           
            The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Civil Aviation would avoid delay in laying of the notifications and in case of any delay
actually taking place in laying , a delay statement is invariably appended.
 
 
(ii) Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion)
 
           
 
      The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion) have
delayed by three months the laying of their notification (Sl. No. 6).  The Ministry have not appended any delay statement even with the
said notification. The Committee hopes that the Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion shall take necessary steps to ensure that
such delay does not recur and in case it is there then the Parliament is kept informed of the reasons therefor through delay statement.
 
(iii)       Ministry of Communications & Information Technology (Department of Telecommunication)
 
            The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Communications & Information Technology (Department of
Telecommunication) have delayed the laying of one of their notification (Sl. 15) by seven months.  The Ministry have appended delay
statement with the notification and the reasons given by the Ministry read thus:
 
      “ The TRAI had sent the regulations to Department of Telecommunications on 21
st February, 2007, after receiving copies of the
regulations in the TRAI on 29th December, 2004 from Controller of Publication, Government of India, after notification of the regulations
in Govt. of India Gazette.  Accordingly there was a delay in laying the regulations on the Table of the House.”
           
            The Committee regrets to note that TRAI had taken around two months to forward the printed copy of the Regulations to the
Department of Telecommunication. But the latter also did not show promptness and the regulations which were received on 21.02.07 were
laid in the Rajya Sabha on 10.05.07. The Committee hope that Department of Telecommunication would take necessary precaution to
ensure that such an instance is not repeated.
 
(iv)   Ministry of Communications & Information Technology (Department of Posts)
 
            The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry have delayed   laying of one of their notification (Sl No.17). The delay

statement accompanying the said notification reads:
 
      “The Gazette Notification was published on 8.8.2006 followed by amendment on 25.10.2006.  As the time between the date on which
copies of the second Gazette Notification were received in the Department and the
 
 
conclusion of the last session (2006) of the both the Houses of Parliament was insufficient, the Notification could not be laid in   time.”
 
            The Committee feels that with a reasonable amount of precautuion the Department of Posts could have safely laid the notification
before the Rajya Sabha during the Winter Session (2006). The Committee hopes that the Department would take necessary steps to ensure
that such delay does not recur.
 
(v)        Ministry of Company Affairs
 
            The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Company Affairs have delayed their notification (Sl. No. 25) and  the
Ministry have also failed to append delay statement  explaining the reasons for such delay on their  part.
 
            The  Committee recommends  that the Ministry  should in future adhere to the laying procedure  and  whenever a delay occurs, the
Parliament is kept informed of the reason for the same by appending a delay statement.
 
           
(vi)       Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue)
 
            The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Finance have delayed in laying their notifications (Sr. Nos.39, 40, 41,42, 43,
44, 45, , 57& 58 64), the delay ranging from 3 to 10 months.  The Ministry have not appended delay statements with the notifications at
(Sl. Nos. 57 and 58).           
 
The Committee regrets to note that the Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs) have delayed the laying of a number
of notifications. The notification at Sl No. 39 carries the date as 27.04.06 and appropriately, it should have been laid in the Monsoon
Session 2007. Having failed to do so the Department of Economic Affairs should not have waited for the second half of the Winter
Session (2007) for sending the papers for laying to the Rajya Sabha Secretariat. If this precaution had been taken, the notification could
have been laid one session earlier. The Committee recommends that the Ministries should take the first available opportunity for laying
their notification during the session.
 
 
(vii)      Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (Department of AYUSH)
 
 
 
The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of  5 months on the part of the Ministry of Health & Family
Welfare(Department of Ayush)  in laying their notification  (Sl. No. 100)
 
            The notification laid on 08.06.06 the Department of AYUSH would have safely laid the same during the Monsoon Session  or
latest in the Winter Session of Parliament, 2006 But the notification was laid only during the Budget Session 2007. The Committee
accordingly recommends that the Department of AYUSH should take necessary corrective steps to ensure that such delay dose not recur
in future. 
 
(viii)      Ministry of Home Affairs
 
The Committee notes with regret the Ministry of Home Affairs have delayed in laying four of their notifications the delay ranging
from 8 months to 10 months (Sl. Nos. 103, 104, 105 & 107) The Ministry have not appended delay  statements with any of these
notifications
 
            The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Home Affairs would avoid such instances of delay in the laying of Subordinate
Legislation and shall in such circumstance keep the House informed of the reasons for delay in laying by appending delay statements.
 
 
(ix)     Ministry of Human Resource Development (Department of Elementary Education & Literacy)
            The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Human Resource Development (Department of Elementary Education &
Literacy) have delayed the laying of their notifications (Sl. Nos. 111, 112, & 113). The delay statements appended with the notification
reads that the Notification was received by this Department on 7.9.2006 i.e. after the completion of Monsoon Session which ended on
23.8.2006.  The Papers were got authenticated by MOS (EE&L) for laying in the winter session of Parliament and sent on 18.12. 2006

170th Report of Committee on Subordinate Legislation
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/170threport.htm[25-10-2016 16:42:40]
However, these were not accepted by Parliament House due to non availability of time of 3 clear days to them before closure of winter
session.
 
            The Committee is unhappy to note that the notifications were received in the Ministry fairly on time, but the Ministry failed to lay
them during the Winter Session 2006. The Committee recommends that Ministry should take the first available opportunity of laying their
statutory notifications and should not tend to postpone this work for the later part of the session so that the eventualities like early
prorogation of the House, which is of course rare, are taken care of.
 
 (ix) (A)    Ministry of Human Resource Development (Department of Higher Education)
 
The Committee notes with concern that the Ministry of Human Resource Development have delayed in laying notifications ranging from
5 months to 10 months.  The Ministry have also failed to append delay statements as well with their notification at (Sl. No. 114) (The
delay statement appended put forth the reason that these are being laid in the earliest Session after receipt of the documents from AICTE.
In future, all efforts will be made to ensure that these documents are laid on the Table of the House in time)
 
            The Committee notes with deep concern the inordinate delay in laying their notification of as much as 17 months.  The Committee
find that the laying of the notifications was delayed due to their late receipt in the Ministry from the AICTE. In this content the Committee
observes that it is the Ministry’s responsibility to ensure that the subordinate Legislation is laid before the Parliament within the prescribed
schedule and accordingly, it is for the Ministry only to ensure that they receive the same timely from the Statutory bodies under them .
The Committee recommends that the Department of Higher Education may take necessary remedial measures to ensure that papers are
received timely in the Ministry from the Statutory bodies.
(x)        Ministry of Labour & Employment (Directorate General of Employment & Training)
            The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Labour & Employment (Directorate General of Employment & Training)
have delayed by 5 months in laying their notification (Sl. No. 121).  Delay statement has been appended with the notification
            The Committee expects the Ministry of Labour & Employment (Directorate General of Employment& Training) to exercise
caution in the matter of timely laying of Subordinate Legislation and ensure that such delays do not recur.
(xi)       Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs
            The Committee notes with dismay that the Ministry have exceptionally delayed the laying of their notifications (Sl. Nos 130,131).
 
 
 
 
The delay in laying the said notifications ranges from 1 year to over 3 years.  The delay statement appended with GSR 143 dated
the 26
th February, 2004  and with  GSR 50 (E) dated 6 February, 2006 reads :
 
            “The work in respect of Emigration was transferred from Ministry of Labour to Indian Overseas Affairs. During this period six
notifications were issued in pursuance of the delegated power under the provisions of Emigration Act, 1983. The officers who monitor
Protector General of Emigration who regulates Emigration Act, 1983, and rules framed thereunder were transferred in haste as a result
thereof, these notifications could not be laid on the Table during this period.
 
            The Committee expresses its unhappiness over the inordinate delay that has taken place in the laying of the two notifications. The
reason for delay tendered by the Ministry do not seem to be very convincing, if seen with reference to the period of delay. The Committee,
accordingly, recommends that the Ministry should take all necessary precaution for future so as to avoid recurrence of such situations.
 
(xii)      Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions (Department of Personnel & Training)
 
            The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Personnel Public Grievances & Pensions (Department of Personnel &
Training) have delayed the laying of one of their notifications (Sl. No. 146) by ten months.  The delay statement appended with the said
notification reads:-
 
            “This notification had not been received in time from the Govt. of India Press due to this reason the same could not be laid on the
Table of Rajya Sabha within stipulated period.”
            The Committee would like to impress upon the Ministry of Personnel that it is their responsibility to ensure that copies of the
notifications are received timely from the Government of India Press and for this purpose they may evolve a suitable mechanism of
check/counter check so that such instances do no recur. The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Personnel would take action
accordingly in order to comply with the prescribed schedule in the matter of laying of Statutory notifications.
 
(xiii)      Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
 
           

170th Report of Committee on Subordinate Legislation
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/170threport.htm[25-10-2016 16:42:40]
 
 
The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas have delayed by 6 months the laying of their
notification (Sl. No. 157). Delay statement is appended with the said notification. 
 
 
            The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas should take necessary remedial steps to ensure that the
Statutory notification is laid timely, as per the prescribed schedule.
 
 
(xiv)     Ministry of Power   
 
            The Committee regrets to note that one notification (Sl. No. 160) laid by the Ministry of Power has been delayed by seven
months.  The Ministry have not appended any delay statement with the said notification.
 
            The Committee hopes that the Ministry would avoid such instances of delay in laying of Subordinate Legislation in future. The
Committee also impress upon the Ministry to take note of the fact that in case there is a delay in the laying of any Statutory notification,
the same should be accompanied by a delay statement while it is being laid.
 
           
(xv)      Ministry of Urban Development
 
            The Committee notes with serious concern that the Ministry of Urban Development have delayed the laying of their notification
(Sl.No. 186) abnormally by 1 year and 3 months.  The delay statement appended to the notification reads;
 
“Copies of the Gazette Notification were received in the Ministry from the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) on 21.11.2006,
and reason for delay was received from DDA on 11.12.2006.  The delay in furnishing the copies of the Gazette Notification by DDA
occurred due to administrative lapses on the part of DDA officials. Suitable action against the defaulting officials is being taken.
 
            The Recruitment Regulations for the post of Asstt. Engineer (Civil/Electrical) in DDA were proposed to be laid on the Table of
both the Houses of Parliament during the winter Session 2006.  However, by the time the papers were ready for laying, the Winter Session
2006 had concluded.  Delay caused in laying these Notifications on the Table of the Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha is regretted.”
 
 
 
The Committee recommends the Ministry of Urban Development to adhere strictly to the schedule as recommended by the
Committee for timely laying of Subordinate Legislation.   The Committee hopes that the Ministry would be able to avoid recurrence of
such instances in future.
 
 
3.     The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take immediate steps to ensure timely and proper laying of
subordinate legislation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Departments of the Government of
India, particularly, the defaulting ones, the following recommendations, as contained in its 131
st,135th  and 152nd Reports:
        “Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session immediately
following the date of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, on the date of the publication of
the Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between the date of publication and the date of the closing of the Session is less
than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said Session. All the Ministries/Departments of
Government of India should henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of the Orders issued under various Acts of
Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.” (131
st Report)
 
        “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential that in case there is a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the
concerned Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay statement along with the notifications being laid so as to apprise

(i)        Ministry of Agro & Rural Industries 
 
          The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of 11 months and 9 months, respectively, in
laying of two notifications (Sl Nos. 1 & 2) and no delay statement was sent therewith.
 
          The Committee would like the Ministry of Agro & Rural Industries to take corrective measures so as to
obviate such delay in future and in case such delays occur the notification while being laid before Parliament
should be accompanied  by statutes giving reason for the delay in laying.
    
(ii)     Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Department of Commerce)
 
          The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Department of Commerce)
have delayed the laying of their notification (Sl. No. 4) by 3 months. The delay statement appended by the said
notification reads:-
 
          “The Coffee Board (Cadre & Recruitment) Rules, 1993 were framed by the Coffee Board in accordance with
the powers conferred by Rule 31 of the Coffee Board Rules, 1955.  As there was no provision under Rule 31 of the
Coffee Rules, 1955 regarding laying of the rules made thereunder, on the table of the Parliament, the same could
not be laid on the Table of each House of Parliament.
 
          However, the Rajya Sabha Committee on Subordinate Legislation were of the view that as per sub-section
(xv) of Section 48 of the Coffee Act, 1942, the rule making powers, in respect of Pay & allowances, leave and
other conditions of the service of the staff employed by the Board (other than those appointed by Central Govt.)
and other employees of the Board, are vested with the Central Govt. and as
such these rules should have been framed by the Central Govt. not by the Coffee Board.”
           The Committee regrets to note that the delay statement gives only the circumstance under which the
required rules have framed/laid but there is nothing in it to explain how the laying of the notification has been
delayed by three months.  The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Department of
Commerce) would take note of discrepancy and avoid recurrence of the same in future.

delay in laying the notification should invariably be accompanied by a delay statement explaining the reasons for
such delay.

3.   The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take immediate steps to ensure timely and
proper laying of subordinate legislation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of all
Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, particularly, the defaulting ones, the following
recommendations, as contained in its 131st,135th  and 152nd Reports:
      “Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session
immediately following the date of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in
Session, on the date of the publication of the Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between the
date of publication and the date of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the
Session immediately following the said Session. All the Ministries/Departments of Government of India should
henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of the Orders issued under various Acts of Parliament
on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.
(131st Report)
(Presented on 15 December 2000)
      “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential that in case there is a delay in the laying of
Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay statement along with the
notifications being laid so as to apprise Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee desires all
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intension is that through the process of formulation of a
delay statement the Ministry is able to introspect, identify bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”.
(135
th Report)
(Presented on 27 July 2001)
 
      “In the opinion of the Committee, every notification should be assigned a distinctive number in order to give it
a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be published/laid which does not carry a notification
number. The Committee expects all Ministries/Departments of Government of India to exercise caution in this
regard. In case where there are more than one notification under a single file, the Ministries/Departments should
ensure that the file number on each notification should be suitably distinguished from one another.
(152nd Report)
     (Presented on 26 August 2004)

I
 
The Edible Oils Packaging (Regulation) Order, 1998.
 
 
          The Edible Oils Packaging (Regulation) Order, 1998 framed under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 was examined
and a questionnaire on the subject was forwarded to the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution,
(Directorate of Vanaspati, Vegetable Oils & Fats) on the 29
th September, 1999 for their comments/clarifications thereon.   The
Ministry vide their O.M. dated the 26 th May, 2000 furnished their comments/clarifications on each point raised in the
questionnaire. The points referred to the Ministry and their comments/clarifications thereon are reproduced below: -

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/172%20Report.htm[25-10-2016 16:42:19]
 
1.       Point raised
Whether the Edible Oils Packaging (Regulation) Order, 1998 has been laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha, if so, the
details in this regard.
Ministry’s Comments
41 copies of the Edible Oils Packaging (Regulation) Order, 1998 issued vide Notification NO. GSR. 584 (E) dated 17-
09-1998 and Corrigendum No. GSR 702 (E) dated 30-11-1998 alongwith one copy of each in Hindi and in English
authenticated by the Minister (Consumer Affairs and Public Distribution) were sent to both Lok Sabha and Rajya  Sabha
Secretariats on 10-12-1998 vide this Directorate’s letter No. 17/1/98-EXP. dated 09-12-1998. While information from Lok
Sabha regarding laying of the papers on the Table on 15-12-1998 (vide Lok Sabha Bulletin Part –I No. 58) has been received,
the information from Rajya Sabha has not be received so far.
 
2.       Point raised- 
Clause 2(b)
          “Edible Oils” mean  vegetable oils and fats and include any i.e, margarine, vanaspati, bakery shorting and fat spread as
specified in the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (37 of 1954) and rules made there under, for human consumption;”
Whether the term “edible oils” include ghee and butter also and if not, the justification for non-inclusion of these items
within the meaning of the term.
Ministry’s Comments
The term “Edible Oils” does not include ghee and butter, as ghee and butter are of animal origin and not of vegetable
origin. The term “edible oils” means vegetable oil as per the definition of “edible oils”
 
3.       Point raised- Clause 2(c)
          “Edible Oils Commissioner” means the person appointed as Edible Oils Commissioner by the Central Government and
includes any other person empowered by the Central Government to exercise any or all of the functions of the Edible Oils
commissioner under this Order;”
Whether there are any qualifications or conditions precedent to empowering any person to exercise any or all the
functions of the Edible Oil Commissioner and if so, whether Government have any objection in prescribing them in the Order
itself.
Ministry’s Comments
No qualification has been explicitly stated. The implicit understanding is that the person empowered to exercise the
functions of the Edible Oils Commissioner would be a Senior Gazetted Officer of the Central/ State Government competent
enough to handle the responsibility of the job assigned and enjoying the confidence of the superiors.
 
Action Taken
Modified the provision of Clause 2 (c) of the Order vide notification dated 22 nd November, 2005 (Annexure VII-
Appendix ‘A’)
 
4.       Point raised- 
Clause 3(b)
          “which is not packed in a container, marked and labeled in the manner as specified in the Scheule-1:
                  Provided that the State Government may, in the public interest, for reasons to be recorded in writing, in specific
circumstances and for a specific period by a notification in the Official Gazette, exempt any edible oil from the provisions of
this Order.”
What is the justification for empowering the State Governments to exempt any edible oil from the provisions of this
Order? What are the specific circumstances in the mind of the Ministry behind prescribing for such exemption? Further, there

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/172%20Report.htm[25-10-2016 16:42:19]
is no provision in the clause under which the State Government is under any obligation to inform the Central Government or
the Edible Oils Commissioner regarding the exemption given to any edible oil. Whether such information is not desirable in the
opinion of Government; what is the reaction of the Ministry in this regard? Whether these provisions are being implemented in
a foolproof manner?
Ministry’s Comments
The Central Government is aware of the fact that the production of edible oils is highly decentralized. Substantial
quantity is produced in the small scale or unorganized sector. Further, a sizeable portion of the population is living below the
poverty line. It is in view of these situations that the State Governments have been empowered to exempt any edible oil from
the provisions of this Order in specific circumstances and for specific period only in the public interest for reasons to be
recorded in writing and for specific period only.
          Further vide 
Clause 15, the Edible Oil Commissioner has been authorized to issue appropriate directions including
seeking of information from the State Governments for the purpose of giving effect to the provisions of the Packaging Order.
 
5.       Point raised- Clause 4(1) read with Schedule-III
“Registration: No person shall carry on business as a packer except under a certificate of registration granted to him
under this Order and in accordance with the terms and conditions specified in the Schedule-III.”
One of the terms and conditions for grant of certificate of registration is that the registered packer shall not employ any
person who is suffering from infection/contagious disease which is likely to affect packing in hygienic conditions. Which is the
authority that would determine whether any particular disease is infectious or contagious; whether Government have any
objection in prescribing the competent authority in the Order itself? Further, it has been made obligatory for each registered
packer to maintain a register showing the quantity sold. Is it not possible that a registered packer may not be engaging himself
in selling, the product and that he might be doing only the packaging work, in that case such a registered packer would not be
able to comply with this condition and he would be unable to keep a record of the edible oil sold. Whether Government have
any objection in suitable modification of this condition? 
Ministry’s Comments
The power for implementation of the Packaging Order is delegated to the State Governments. It has been left to the State
Governments to decide as to how they will carry-out the various provisions of the order. We have already written to the State
Governments that in case there is any operational difficulty in the implementation of the Order, these may be brought to the
notice of the Central Government so as to resolve the issue in a manner which is not inconsistent with the provisions of this

          When these regulations were framed in 1975, there was no provision in the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 for
placing of regulations before both Houses of Parliament.  This requirement was introduced by insertion of provision by
Act 17 of 1982 with effect from 31.5.1982.
Committee’s observation
          The Committee was appraised that the regulations were not laid on the table of both the Houses as there was no
laying provision in the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 prior to 1982.  The Committee desired that the regulations should
be laid now alongwith the amendments suggested by it.
(2)     Point referred: Regulation 1 (2)

Ministry’s reply
          Section 124 (1) of the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 provides that no regulation made by the Board under the Act
(other than a regulation made under sub-section 2 of section 17) shall have effect until it has been approved by the
Central Government and until such approval has been published in the Official Gazette.   The provision in the
regulation is accordingly worded for the regulations to come into effect from date of publication of Government’s
sanction in the Gazette.   In effect, however, the regulations came into effect from the date of publication in the
Gazette.
Committee’s observation
          The management of the board had agreed to amend the commencement clause as suggested by the Committee.

6.       Point raised
Schedule-III
For appointment to the posts in the Schedule, the method of promotion has been stated to be on the basis of
seniority-cum-merit.
What are the main features of this procedure for promotion; Whether it is permissible to change the seniority of
officials as it exists in the feeder grade while recommending their names for promotion to the next higher grade which
is inherent in the “selection” as a method of promotion at least for the purpose of promotion in scale III, scale II and
scale I so as to promote merit in the organisation?
Ministry’s reply
“Seniority-cum-merit” shall mean seniority and found fit for promotion.   It is not possible to change the
seniority of officials, as it exists in the feeder grade.  Thus, seniority-cum-merit implies promotions based on seniority
subject to minimum necessary merit requisite for the promotion.  The Government feels that there should be a uniform
criterion for promotion to all scales and that the present system may continue.
Committee’s Observation
The Committee came across divergent views on the point of promotion on the basis of seniority-cum-merit.  The
Bank of Rajasthan was of the view that promotion should not be purely on the basis of seniority only and merit should
also be given at least 50% weight age.  The Dungarpur Banswara Gramin Bank was of the view that in lower scales,
weight age may be given to seniority but in higher scale merit should prevail.   The Gramin Bank was of the view that
promotion should be made on the basis of both seniority and merit.  The Committee reiterated the need for balance
between seniority and merit to keep the Regional Rural Banks competitive with the other commercial banks.
Action taken
The existing recruitment rules provide for filling up the posts by seniority-cum-merit.   It, therefore, gives due
weightage to the seniority as well as merit.    However, the position would be reviewed after the process for
amalgamation is completed.

regulations to come into effect on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette which is the normal format

regulation 8 (2). The Committee had expressed its desire that the fee for a pilot’s licence should be revised
suitably and in case no fee is charged, the provision being irrelevant should be scrapped.
(iii)     By replacing the words “assist in instructing” with the words “assist and instruct” in the pre revised (1975)
regulations 25 thereby, making the provision more clear and specific.

were not relevant to the current times and were obsolete. Regulation 33 of the 1975 regulations provided that
pilots may leave vessels at anchor in the harbour if not provided with proper food and sleeping accommodation.

more relevant to the current times and also complied with the requirement of laying the regulations before the
Parliament which could not be done in the case of 1975 regulations due to the absence of such a provision in the Major
Port Trusts Act, 1963.

secured creditor, as the case may be.

secured creditor in this regard?
 
          Ministry’s 
comments : (7.5. 2004)
Approved valuer means the professional who is qualified to value the property for a fee.  It is difficult to
work out clear-cut definition making exhaustive list of approved valuers  in different fields and types of properties

Government under Rule 8C of the Wealth Tax Act and also by CBDT.
 
 
Action Taken by the 
Ministry : (29.11.2006)
In terms of Rule 8(5) of Security Enforcement Rules, 2002, before effecting sale of immovable property, the

the secured creditor, fix the reserve price of the property.  Chapter VII-B (Section 34 AB) of Wealth Tax Act, 1957

          IRDA has reported that details of number of posts, their classification, scale of pay, age limit,
education and other qualification, period of probation, method of recruitment, composition of selection

(a)     Merit, suitability and seniority in cases of Class I and II posts:

'merit' and seniority are the words that are used; what is the justification for deviations from general
guidelines of Government of India in case of promotions?
Ministry’s Comments
:- (14/03/2002)
          IRDA has reported that word "suitability" has been included deliberately in the regulations as a

      The Determination of the Price of the Forfeited Property Rules, 2005  
 
 The Determination of the Price of the Forfeited Property Rules, 
2005 framed under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 were 
examined and certain points, which needed further 
comments/clarifications, were put together in the form of a questionnaire. 
It was forwarded to the Ministry of Home Affairs for their 
comments/clarifications on July 10, 2006.  In reply, the Ministry of Home 
Affairs vide their communication dated October 16, 2006 informed as 
follows :- 
“….that the comments of Rajya Sabha Secretariat 
were examined and draft   comments were sent to the 
Ministry of Law for vetting.  The Ministry of Law has 
accepted the comments of Ministry of Home Affairs in Rule 
6.  The Comments in Rule 3, 5(1), 5(2), 7(1) and 7(2) have 
been reexamined and fresh comments of this Ministry are 
enclosed. 
 
On receipt of the Rajya Sabha acceptance on the 
proposed comments/amendments, the approval of Hon’ble 
Home Minister will be obtained for notifying the same.” 
 
2. The   points   referred to the Ministry and their comments thereon 
are reproduced below : 
 
1.     Point raised:  Rule 3 : Appointment of Authorised Officer  
“Where the person against whom an order of forfeiture has been 
made (hereinafter referred to as the person), is acquitted, the property 
shall  be returned to him or his legal nominee and if it is not possible for 
any reason to return the forfeited property, the State Government shall 

appoint an officer not below the rank of Deputy Secretary to that 
Government, to be known as Authorised Officer, to evaluate and fix the 
price of the forfeited property with a view to compensating the person in 
lieu of the forfeited property.” 
As per Rule 3, all what has been said about the Authorised Officer 
is that he must not be below the rank of Deputy Secretary of the 
Government. As the job of evaluation is technical, should the Authorised 
Officer not possess some technical qualification also? 
 
 
Ministry's reply: 
In order to have a more cogent procedure for the authorized officer 
to compute the value of forfeited property, it is proposed that Rule 3 
may be amended by inserting an explanation which will allow the 
Authorized Officer to utilize the service of consultant(s)/Valuer(s) to 
arrive at the value of forfeited property. 
 
2.    Point raised: Rule 5 : Consideration of the representation : 
          "(1) The Authorised Officer shall take into account, representation, 
if any, made by the person or his leg al nominee before the final 
determination of the price with respect to the forfeited property is made" 
 Whether the Ministry have any objection in specifying a time frame 
for disposal of representation, if any, given by the person or his legal 
nominee or f or that matter for completing the whole process of 
determining the price of the forfeited property under the rules? 
 
Ministry's reply 

 180 days from the first day of the next month of the receipt of the 
representation. 
 
3.    Point raised: Rule 5: Consideration of the representation: 
 
          "(2) The Authorised Officer shall thereafter fix the price of the 
forfeited property and intimate the same in writing to the person or his 
legal nominee". 
 Rule 5 mentions that the Authorised Officer shall intimate the person 
or his legal nominee as to the fixing of the price of the forfeited property. 
Rule 6 maintains that the State Government should issue an order to the 
effect that the property stands sold to the State Government at the price 
fixed under rule 5. 
        Whether the intimation to the person/legal nominee is accompanied 
by such an order, or such an arrangement is being viewed as an assurance 
to the concerned individual. 
Ministry's reply: 
 Within 60 days from the date the proces s of determining the price of 
forfeited property is completed. 
 The persons/legal nominee is informed about the price of the forfeited 
property as per Rule 5(2) of the said Act. Further reference by the State 
Government to the Central Government about the Head of Account etc. 
is an administrative function only.  The M/o Law and Justice have opined 
that this appears to be sustainable. 
 
4.    Point raised : Rule 7: Deposit of the amount by the Central 
Government: 
 

           " (1) The Central Government shall on receipt of the order under 
rule 6, deposit the price fixed for the forfeited property in such Treasury 
or under such Head of Account as may be specified therein under 
intimation to the person or his legal nominee." 
 As the matter being of utmost urgency  to the affected individual, 
whether the Ministry have any objection in specifying a time -frame 
within which the Central Government, after receipt of such an order as 
specified in rule 6, deposit the forfeited property in such Treasury under 
such Head of A ccount as specified in such an order under intimation to 
the person or his legal nominee.   
 
Ministry's reply: 
 Within 30 days from the date of order as specified in Rule 6. 
 
5.    Point raised: Rule 7: Deposit of the amount by the Central 
Government: 
 
           " (2) The amount of price along with interest there on, shall be paid 
to the person  
Or to his legal nominee."  
   
           Sub-rule (2) of Rule 7 mentioned about payment of the price of the 
forfeited property along with "interest thereon". Wheth er Ministry will 
specify at what rate interest will be paid to the claimant? 
 
 
 
Ministry's reply: 

 It is proposed that the interest may be paid at the prevailing interest 
rates on savings bank account of State Bank of India.  
 
The Committee considered the replies of the Ministry of Home 
Affairs on the points forwarded to them.  The Committee notes with 
satisfaction that the Ministry of Home Affairs have agreed to take action 
as follows in pursuance to its suggestions : 
(i) In Rule 3, to insert  an explanation allowing  the Authorized 
Officer to utilize the service of consultant(s)/Valuer(s) to 
arrive at the value of forfeited property.  In the existing rules, 
the Authorised Officer is required to do this job  without any  
assistance; and   
(ii) In Rule  7 (2), to  make provision for paying  the interest at 
the prevailing interest rates on savings bank account of State 
Bank of India on the price of the forfeited property to the 
claimant.  The existing provisions do no mention about  the 
rate of interest. 
 The Committee hopes that the Ministry would carry out the above 
amendments expeditiously under intimation to it. However, on other 
points, the Committee notes with satisfaction the reply given by  the 
Ministry of Home Affairs.

They had also asked for the acceptance of this Secretariat on the

The Committee, in its meeting held on 22 nd November, 2007,

(ii) In Rule  7 (2), by paying  the interest at the prevailing interest

 However, on other points, the Committee was satisfied with the replies

 The acceptance of the above proposal was communicated to the
