THE TEA (DISTRIBUTION AND EXPORT) CONTROL ORDER, 2005 
 
 The Tea (Distribution and Export) Control Order, 2 005 ( Annexure I ) has been 
framed under the Tea Act, 1953 ( Annexure II ). This Order has been framed superseding 
the Tea (Distribution and Export) Control Order, 19 57, and seeks to ensure that all tea 
consignments meant for imports or exports would hav e to undergo a certification 
procedure under which the quality of tea and the co untry of its origin would be 
determined and displayed. The Tea Board has been de signated the nodal agency for this 
certification exercise. Further, the non-preferenti al certification of origin of each 
consignment of tea exports would be issued by the T ea Board or any of its designated 
agencies. The basic objective of this Order is to retain the brand equity of Indian tea.  
 
2. The Committee took up for examination of the sai d Rules and a questionnaire was 
forwarded to the  Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce & Industry on 22 
nd  
May, 2007. The Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce & Industry furnished 
their comments/clarifications on the points raised in the questionnaire (Annexure III) . 
The points raised by the Committee and the comments  of the Ministry are reproduced 
below: 
 
I  Framing of the Tea (Distribution and Export) Control, 2005  
 The Committee wanted to know about the reasons for  framing the Tea 
(Distribution and Export) Control Order, 2005 which  has been framed in supersession of 
the Tea (Distribution and Export) Control Order, 19 57, the major points of distinction 
between the Orders of 1957 and 2005, and the salient feature of the new Order? 
In response the Ministry informed the Committee tha t the new control order were 
framed in supersession of the earlier Tea (Distribu tion and Export) Control Order, 1957 
for strengthening the surveillance work of the Tea Board, to ensure standard of quality of 
tea for export/import and to maintain image of Indi an tea in the overseas market. The 
main reasons  to frame the Order and objectives thereof are as follows: 

(1) Reports of poor quality teas being imported and its  impact on domestic tea 
industry as well as on export of tea from India. 
(2) Reports of export of non-Indian tea  under a cover of a certificate of Indian 
origin tea . 
(3) Non-conformity of imported tea with the standard of  quality of tea as per ISO 
3720 leading to disrepute Indian Tea, thereby adver sely affecting India tea 
exports. 
(4) Order of the Kerala High Court exempting applicability of the Prevention of Food 
Adulteration Act for the teas stored for export. 
(5) Absence of any general rule defining “Indian Tea” f or the purpose of its export 
from India to other countries. 
 
 The salient features of the new order are as follows: 
 
(1) To ensure the standard of quality of tea meant for import /export 
(2) Issue of non-preferential certificate of origin tow ards export of tea from India by 
the agencies approved by Tea Board. 
(3) Stipulation of details of rules of origin for issua nce of certificate of Origin for 
export of tea from India to any country. 
(4) Stipulation of provision for obtaining business lic ence who will be engaged in 
business of distribution of imported tea. 
(5) Stipulation of provision towards import and distribution of tea.  
(6) Mandatory stipulation towards ensuring conformity o f tea to specification of tea 
in respect of export of tea or export of imported tea.  
 
II Rule 1(2) Short Title and Commencement :- 
 
 It shall come into force, on the date of its publi cation in the Official Gazzette, 
(except paragraph 8, paragraph 11 and clause (d), ( e), & (f) of paragraph 21 which shall 
come into force on the expiry of sixty days on and from the date of its said publication 
and paragraph 22 which shall come into force on exp iry of thirty days of said 
publication). 

 
 The Committee took note of the fact that Rule 1(2)  states that paragraph 8, 11 and 
clause (d), (e), & (f) of paragraph 21 which shall come into force on the expiry of sixty 
days on and from the date of its said publication o f the Tea (Distribution & Export) 
Control Order, 2005 and paragraph 22 on the expiry of thirty days from the date of the 
said publication. It enquired whether these paragra phs had come into force or not. It also 
asked to provide details in either case. The Commit tee also wanted to know the 
logic/objectives behind allowing more time before implementing certain provisions of the 
Order from later dates and whether those objectives have been achieved? 
 
The Ministry stated that paragraph 8, 11 and clause  (d), (e), & (f) of paragraph 21 
had come into force immediately on expiry of sixty days from the date of publication of 
the Order in the official gazette i.e. from 1 
st  April, 2005. Similarly, paragraph 22 had also 
come into force on expiry of thirty days from 1 st  April, 2005. 
 
Paragraph 8 is in relation to grant and refusal of business licence in favour of 
exporter and paragraph 11 is in relation to grant a nd refusal of non-preferential certificate 
of origin. In case of business licence to exporter it may be mentioned that under the 
earlier Order of 1957, number of firms had obtained  such licence either for temporary 
period or on permanent basis. Since nobody can expo rt tea unless he obtains licence from 
Tea Board under the Tea (Distribution and Export) C ontrol Order, 2005, there is a need 
to allow time to the intending exporter to obtain licence from Tea Board as per conditions 
stipulated in paragraph 8. It may also be mentioned  that the licensed tea exporters under 
the order of 1957, have been allowed to export tea till the validity period indicated in the 
licence granted under the said Order of 1957. This relaxation has been granted after 
obtaining approval of the Central Government.  
 
 As regards paragraph 11, clause (d), (e), & (f) of  paragraph 21 and paragraph 22, 
it was mentioned that they are new provisions. 
 The reasons for allowing more time before implemen tation of certain provisions 
is that in the case of these provisions, the export ers who had licenses under the earlier 
order needed extra time before coming within the purview of the new Order.  

 
III  Other Rules & Orders issued under the Tea Act, 195 3 
 
The Committee raised the fact that the Tea (Distribution & Export) Control Order, 
2005 has replaced the Tea (Distribution & Export) C ontrol Order, 1957. Similarly, the 
Tea (Marketing) Control Order, 1998 has been replac ed by the Order of 2003. In this 
respect what is the status with regard to other rul es/regulations/Orders framed under the 
Tea Act, 1953, like the Tea Rules, 1954, the Tea (W aste) Control Order, 1959 etc. which 
have become quite old? Whether Government would con siders reviewing these and other 
Orders under the Tea Act and update them accordingly. 
 
 The Ministry took note of the concern of the Commi ttee and informed that the 
Tea (Marketing) Control Order 1984 has been replace d by the Order of 2003 and the Tea 
(Distribution & Export) Control Order, 1957 has bee n replaced by the Order of 2005. At 
present Ministry is examining the different provisi ons of Tea Act 1953 and Tea Rules 
made thereunder so that the same can be substituted  by the new Act and Rules in view of 
liberalization and globalization era. The Committee  was informed that two committees 
have been constituted to look into different provis ions of the Tea Waste (Control) Order 
1959 and the Tea Warehouses (Licensing) Order 1989 for modification/amendment, if 
necessary. 
 The Committee feels that India occupies a leading p osition in tea export and 
therefore all efforts should be made to ensure that  it’s eminent position is 
maintained. It accordingly urges the Ministry to up date the concerned Acts and 
Orders at the earliest, if it has not been done til l now, so as to provide a strong 
statutory basis aligned to the current global scenario. 
 
IV Rule 8(4): Grant and refusal of business licence/pe rmanent licence to 
exporters- 
 The Licensing Authority may refuse to grant a perma nent business licence to any 
applicant and shall furnish him with a copy of the order so passed: 
 Provided that before passing an order of refusal a n opportunity of being heard 
shall be granted to the applicant . 

 The Committee was of the view that the rule provid es the applicant an 
opportunity to be heard before being refused a perm anent business licence along with 
furnishing him with a copy of such order. Therefore  does the Government have any 
objection in providing the reasons to be recorded in writing and issue of speaking order in 
case an applicant is refused grant of a business li cence besides giving him an opportunity 
to be heard. 
 
In reply the Department stated the following: 
For implementation of paragraph 8, the following procedure is being adopted: 
Examination of documents furnished by the applicant 
Recording of reasons in writing in case the applicant is considered to be refused to 
grant a business license and the said reasons are r equired to be communicated to 
applicant to enable him to overcome the defects so indicate in writing. 
In case the applicant overcomes the defect the busi ness licence is granted and in 
case the defects are not taken care of fully he is given an opportunity of being 
heard and on the basis of the hearing by the Licens ing Authority, final order of 
refusal, if any, is communicated to the applicant. 
 However Government of India may not have any objec tion to issue speaking 
order in which ground of refusal of license is recorded in cases of rejection. 
The Committee after considering the comments of the  Ministry recommends 
that the Order be amended to include a speaking ord er for recording the ground of 
a refusal of license in cases of rejection . It would provide more transparency to the 
working of the Order . 
 
V  Rule 8(5) :   Where an application for permanent business licence  is not refused 
under sub paragraph 4. the Licensing Authority shal l grant the applicant a permanent 
business licence in form G. 
 The Committee observed that the rule does not spec ify the time frame within 
which a permanent business licence shall be granted  to the applicant from the date of his 
applying for such licence. The Ministry stated that  time frame has not been indicated 
either in paragraph 8(2) or 8(5) in view of the pro cedure adopted by Tea Board and the 
time taken by the applicant in responding to query of the Tea Board. It may be mentioned 

that during the last two years, Tea Board did no re ceive any complaint about the delay in 
granting business licence/permanent business licenc e. The Committee accepted the 
clarification furnished by the Ministry. However as  a way of caution to prevent 
delays the Committee recommends that the Department  should make a study of the 
appropriate time within which the required formalit ies can be completed and the 
should then be incorporated in the Order.  
 
VI  Rule 10(2): Grant and refusal of Certificate of Ori gin for teas designated as 
Geographical Indications. 
 
Where an application for Certificate of Origin is n ot refused under sub paragraph 
(1) the Licensing Authority or any officer of the B oard not below the rank of Joint 
Controller of Licensing duly authorized by the Lice nsing Authority after being satisfied 
that the application is in conformity with the requ irement as laid down under paragraph 5 
and contractual obligation which the applicant has with an importer of such tea, may 
issue a Certificate of Origin of tea to the application Form I. 
In response to the Committee’s  query whether the t ime period within which a 
Certificate of Origin has to be granted by the licencing Authority or the authorized officer 
of the Board in case the same is not refused under sub paragraph (i) of Rule 10(1) should 
not be specified in the rule itself, the Ministry s tated that although the time frame in 
issuing Certificate of Origin is not mentioned the same is being issued within twenty-four 
hours from the time of receipt of application. Till  date Tea Board has not received any 
complaint about the delay in issuance of such certificate. 
The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry is sues the Certificate of 
Origin within twenty four hours. However, the Commi ttee feels that it would be 
more appropriate if the same is reflected in the  O rder and would therefore 
recommend that time frame should be incorporated in the Order itself. 
VII Rule 11(2): Grant and refusal of Non-Preferential Certificate of Origin . 
 Provided that whenever the approved inspection agen cy issues a Certificate of 
Origin to any business licence, a duplicate copy of  the same along with all other 
supporting documents shall be furnished to the Lice nsing Authority or to any other 
officer of the Board duly authorized by Licensing A uthority in this regard, by the said 

inspection agency within twenty-four hours from the  time of issue of such Certificate of 
Origin. 
 The Committee enquired as to what could be the 'su pporting documents' referred 
to in the Rule: Whether Government have any objecti on for providing in the rule itself 
the documents to be furnished to the Licensing Auth ority if the same are required to be 
furnished to the Licensing Authority within 24 hours from the issue of the Certificate. 
 
 The Department clarified that paragraph 11(2) rela tes to grant of non-preferential 
certificate of origin in respect of any consignment  of tea for export based on the 
documents furnished by the applicant. While non-preferential certificate of origin is being 
issued as per Form -E the duplicate copy of the sam e is required to be forwarded to Tea 
Board. The rules of Certificate of Origin has been attached to Form -E wherein it has 
been mentioned that tea not wholly produced or obta ined in India is also eligible to cover 
by a Certificate of Origin with the word either ‘In dia Tea’ (not less than 90% by weight 
of tea) or by the words blended tea of different or igin and packed in India. The 
supporting documents based on which the agency issu es such type of non-preferential 
Certificate of Origin are required to be forwarded to Tea Board. Since the form and 
format of these documents may undergo changes from time to time it may not be suitable 
to specify them in the rule itself. 
The Committee accepts the comments of the Ministry but would like to 
recommend that the process of submission of documen ts may be made on-line and 
the forms required to be submitted may be done in s oft copy along with the scanned 
copies of the required documents. This would not on ly save time but would be more 
transparent and time saving method based on the latest technology .  
VIII Rule 12(1): Period of validity of business licence - 
Every business licence for an exporter shall be val id for a period of three years 
from the date of its issue and every business licence once renewed shall also remain valid 
for a further period of three years from the date o f its renewal unless the business licence 
is cancelled or suspended during the validity period . 
The Committee felt that the validity period of 3 ye ars for a business licence 
appeared to be short, and wanted to know whether Go vernment have any objection in 

increasing the validity period from 3 years to 5 ye ars with a further validity period of 3 
years after its renewal. 
The Committee was informed that at present there ar e two types of business 
licence (1) business licence with a validity period  of three years and (2) permanent 
business licence which is valid till the same is su spended/cancelled or otherwise. At this 
stage the validity period of the business licence i s three years within which the licensee 
has the opportunity to convert their licence to a p ermanent one on the basis of its 
performance. The permanent business licence is gran ted only to the business licence 
holder who have satisfied the eligibility criteria as indicated in paragraph 8(3) of the 
Order. In case the business licensee does not fulfi ll the said criteria, the said business 
licensee has the opportunity to renew the same for another period of three years under 
paragraph 14 of the Order. While the regular export er has converted their business 
licence to permanent business licence, the occasion al exporters have the validity period 
of three years. 
The Committee accepts the comments of the Ministry but requests it to 
ensure that no business licence holder is adversely affected  due to paucity of time . 
 
IX Rule 14(2): Renewal of business licence  
 
Every licencee being an exporter whose business lic ence has been converted into 
a permanent business licence under sub-paragraph (5 ) of paragraph 8, shall not be 
required to renew his business licence. 
The Committee raised the issue that Rule 14(2) prov ides for conversion of 
business into business licence. Under the circumsta nce, whether an exporter can keep a 
business licence in addition to his business licenc e as may be inferred from Rule 14(2). 
Does the conversion into a permanent business licen ce not render the business licence 
defunct, automatically. 
In response the Ministry stated that there is no sc ope for an exporter to keep a 
business licence in addition to his permanent busin ess licence. In fact, the exporter 
having business licence and fulfilling the criteria  indicated in para 8(3) of the Order are 
only eligible to convert his business licence to a permanent business licence. 
 
X Rule 17 (a) and (b): Fees for exporters  

 
 The Committee wanted to know whether Government hav e any objection in 
increasing the validity period from 3 years to 5 ye ars with subsequent renewal validity 
period of 3 years. 
 
 The Ministry informed that at this stage the valid ity period of the business licence 
is three years within which the licensee has the op portunity to convert his licence to a 
permanent one on the basis of its performance. 
 
The Committee took into consideration the clarifica tion furnished by the 
Ministry and also the fact that the last few years had been quite tough for Tea 
exporters. It was of the opinion that the validity period should be increased to five 
years to provide some more time to the licensee to convert his licence to a 
permanent one. 
 
XI Rule 18(2): Conditions of business licence  
 
 Where a business licensee sells or otherwise transf ers his business to another 
person the purchaser or transferee as the case may be, shall obtain a fresh business 
licence in accordance with the provisions of this Order . 
 
 Clarification was sought on whether there are any rules governing the 
sale/transfer of business from one business license e to another person; If not, what is the 
mechanism in place for regulating such sale/transfe r. In response it was informed that the 
business licence is not transferable. However, the infrastructure of a business licence 
holder is transferable as per common law. In such c ase, transferee is required to obtain 
fresh business licence as per para 8 of the Order and guidelines prepared by Tea Board. 
 
XII   Rule 18(3): Provision of Business Licence  
The Committees observed that while the Rule provide s 30 days reporting time to the 
business Licensee in case he enters into a partners hip with another person in business, no 
time period has been specified for the Licensing Au thority to grant the amended business 
licence. Further, whether any fee is charged for amending the business licence: if so, both 
the time period and amount of fees may be specified  in the Rules itself.  In reply, the 

Ministry stated that while the business licensee is  required to intimate the Licensing 
Authority in respect of change of the status of the  firm within thirty days, the amendment 
of the business licence can only be done if the doc uments to that effect are submitted to 
Licensing Authority. Generally such amendment is do ne within 7 days from the date of 
submission of all such documents. Further more, no fee is charged for amendment of 
business licence.  
 
XIII Rule 19(8) states “ Every business licensee shall carry out the directi ons of the 
licensing  Authority within the period as specified by the Licensing Authority ”  
  
 The Committee felt that the rule gives discretiona ry powers to the Licensing 
Authority for specifying the time period for carryi ng out its directions. Therefore, a fixed 
time period for the purpose of the rule may be specified in the Rule itself. 
 
The Ministry stated that the time frame for complia nce of the direction is 
dependent on the nature of directive issued by the Licensing Authority time to time. 
Specifying a fixed time period is not reasonable as  the nature of directive varies and the 
compliance time may also vary. 
 
XIV Rule 21 Explanations (2) and Rule 22 Explanations (2)  
 
 
 The Committee observed that the rule mentions the various types/mixtures of tea, 
which may render it as "adulterated”.  The Committe e, accordingly, wanted to know  the 
fate of such adulterated tea and whether there are rules governing the disposal of such 
adulterated tea. The Ministry informed that such ad ulterated tea cannot be termed as tea 
and it is considered as ‘tea waste’. Disposal of su ch tea waste is guided under the 
provisions of Tea Waste (Control) Order 1959.  
 
The Committee took note of the fact that disposal o f tea waste was been 
governed by Tea Waste (Control) Order, 1959. It was  of the opinion that lots of new 
technologies had come up since the Tea Waste (Contr ol) Order, 1959 was framed. It 
therefore, reiterates that the Ministry should take  a comprehensive view of the Tea 

Act and its concerned subordinate legislation and r edraft them in the current 
perspective .  
 
XV.  Rule 26: Power to register the export contract   
 
Licensing Authority or any Officer of the Board, not below the rank of Joint Controller of 
Licensing duly authorized by the licensing Authorit y, may register the export contract as 
per the procedure to be stipulated by the Licensing Authority from time to time before the 
shipment of tea from India under such export contract .” 
 The Committee observed that the rule gives discret ionary powers to the Licensing 
Authority in the procedure of registering the expor t contract and enquired whether there 
are any rules governing the procedure of registration of export contracts, if so, what is the 
justification for giving such discretionary powers to the Licensing Authority, which are 
liable to be misused. In response the Committee was  informed that this is an enabling 
provision. Provisions of export contracts may vary from country to country. The 
procedure for registration of such export contract can only be stipulated separately for 
different countries as and when required. The regis tration of export contract will enable 
Tea Board to ensure its compliance by the exporter. 
 
XVI  Rule 29: Taking of samples 
 
 The Licensing Authority may take or authorize any o fficer of the Tea board. not 
below the rank of Inspector or any inspection agency to take any sample of not more than 
one kilogram in weight drawn from any stock of tea for the purpose of ascertaining 
whether such sample confirms to the requirements la id down for tea or whether such 
sample conforms to the rules of origin for the purp ose of issuing Certificate of Origin 
and/or to ensure conformity with any or all the pro visions of this Order. No charge shall 
be payable for taking the samples . 
 The Committee noted that the rule provides for tak ing of samples by any 
inspecting agency for the purpose of the rule clari fication was sought whether 
Government have any objection in authorizing some i nspecting agencies for the purpose 
of the rule and the list of such authorized inspecting agencies to be notified in the Gazette 
of India. In response the Ministry clarified that T ea board has already approved eleven 

inspection agencies and the list of which has been circulated among the tea industry. The 
list is also available in Tea Board's website. 
 
XVII Rule 36: Power to approve inspection agency   
 
 The Licensing Authority may approve agencies to inspect the tea meant for export 
on their credential through a Technical Committee constituted by the Licensing Authority 
for this purpose…. . 
 
 Information was sought regarding the composition o f the Technical Committee: 
whether there are any rules governing the compositi on, terms, tenure and functions of the 
Technical Committee. 
 
 In was informed that the Technical Committee was c onstituted by the Chairman, 
Tea board for the purpose of approval of inspection  agency based on the facilities 
available with them. Technical Committee was constituted in April 2005 with following: 
 Dy. Chairman, Tea Board -Chairman of the Committee  
 Adviser, National Tea Research Foundation -Member  
 Director, Research, Tea Board - Member  
 
 The Committee notes that the Ministry did not stat e whether the concerned 
rules governing the composition, terms, tenure and functions of the Technical 
Committee had been framed. The Committee is of the opinion that it would be 
appropriate that necessary subordinate legislation should be framed in this regard, 
if these Technical Committees are of a permanent nature . 
 
XVIII Rule 37: Power to approve tea tasters for constituting a panel 
 
 The Committee raised the issue that this rule give s power to the Licensing 
Authority to approve tea tasters for constituting a  panel for tea tasting. However, the rule 
also provides the Licensing Authority with discreti onary powers to specify the validity 
period for grant of approval to a tea taster to ser ve on the panel or to cancel the approval 
granted to any such tea taster before the expiry of  the validity period. Whether 
Government have any objection in specifying in the rule itself the validity period of the 

panel and for having the reasons to be recorded in writing in case the approval granted to 
a tea taster is cancelled before the expiry of the validity period. 
 
 In response the Ministry stated that the panel of tea taster is to undertake 
organolyptic taste of tea. The Government may not h ave objection to the proposal 
mentioned above. 
 
The Committee is happy that the Ministry has accept ed its suggestion 
regarding specifying in the rule itself the validit y period of the panel and for 
recording reasons in writing in case the approval g ranted to a tea taster is cancelled 
before the expiry of the validity period. It hopes that the Ministry would expedite 
the process of amending the Order to incorporate th e recommendations of the 
Committee. 
 
3. The Committee thereafter took up for discussion the  Order at Darjeeling with the 
representatives of Tea Board along with the Departm ent of Commerce, Ministry of 
Commerce & Industry on 1 
st  June, 2007 and also at Udhagamandalam on 28 th  May, 2008. 
During the said discussions the Committee raised the issue of passing the benefits of high 
prices of Indian Tea to the farmers so that their m otivation and morale is maintained. The 
Committee expressed concern that the benefits of th e high prices did not pass on to the 
farmers.. The Committee raised a number of issues l ike poor working conditions of 
workers engaged in tea plantations; lack of proper implementation of modern tea 
processing technologies. The Committee urged the Mi nistry to look into the prospects of 
spreading tea cultivation to new areas in the North  East which has an environment 
suitable for tea cultivation. The Ministry informed the Committee about the steps taken to 
increase the domestic demand for tea, which has been declining in the last few years. The 
Committee expressed the hope that the efforts made would help the country regain its 
position on the international market. Relevant extr acts of the study note are annexed

Orders at the earliest, if it has not been done til l now, so as to provide a strong 
statutory basis aligned to the current global scenario. 
 
6. Rule 8(4): Grant and refusal of business licence /permanent licence to 
exporters  
The Committee after considering the comments of the  Ministry recommends 
that the Order be amended to include a speaking ord er for recording the ground of 
a refusal of license in cases of rejection . It would provide more transparency to the 
working of the Order 
 
7. Rule 8(5) : The Committee accepted the clarification furnished by the 
Ministry. However as a way of caution to prevent de lays the Committee 
recommends that the Department should make a study of the appropriate time 
within which the required formalities can be comple ted and the should then be 
incorporated in the Order.  
 
8. Rule 10(2): Grant and refusal of Certificate of Origin for teas designated as 
Geographical Indications. 
 The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry i ssues the Certificate of 
Origin within twenty four hours: However, the Commi ttee feels that it would be 
more appropriate if the same is reflected in the  O rder and would therefore 
recommend that time frame should be incorporated in the Order itself. 
 
9. Rule 11(2): Grant and refusal of Non-Preferential Certificate of Origin 
The Committee accepts the comments of the Ministry but would like to recommend 
that the process of submission of documents may be made on-line and the forms 
required to be submitted may be done in soft copy a long with the scanned copies of 

the required documents. This would not only save ti me but would be more 
transparent and time saving method based on the latest technology 
10. Rule 12(1): Period of validity of business lice nce 
 The Committee accepts the comments of the Ministry  but requests it 
to ensure that no business licence holder is adversely affected due to paucity of time . 
 
10 . Rule 17 (a) and (b): Fees for exporters 
The Committee took into consideration the clarifica tion furnished by the 
Ministry and also the fact that the last few years had been quite tough for Tea 
exporters. It was of the opinion that the validity period should be increased to five 
years to provide some more time to the licensee to convert his licence to a 
permanent one. 
 
11. Rule 21 Explanations (2) and Rule 22 Explanatio ns (2) 
 The Committee took note of the fact that disposal of tea waste was 
been governed by Tea Waste (Control) Order, 1959. It was of the opinion that lots of 
new technologies had come up since the Tea Waste (C ontrol) Order, 1959 was 
framed. It therefore, reiterates that the Ministry should take a comprehensive view 
of the Tea Act and its concerned subordinate legisl ation and redraft them in the 
current perspective .  
12. Rule 36: Power to approve inspection agency   
 
 The Committee notes that  the Ministry did not stat e whether the concerned 
rules governing the composition, terms, tenure and functions of the Technical 
Committee had been framed. The Committee is of the opinion that it would be 
appropriate that necessary subordinate legislation should be framed in this regard, 
if these Technical Committees are of a permanent nature. 
 
13. Rule 37: Power to approve tea tasters for const ituting a panel  
 The Committee is happy that the Ministry has accep ted its suggestion 
regarding specifying in the rule itself the validit y period of the panel and for 
recording reasons in writing in case the approval g ranted to a tea taster is cancelled 
before the expiry of the validity period. It hopes that the Ministry would expedite 

the process of amending the Order to incorporate th e recommendations of the 
Committee. 
 
14. The Committee is hopeful that the Ministry woul d carry out the 
recommendations  of the Committee expeditiously und er intimation to it. The 
Committee is also of the opinion that proper monito ring and inspections are 
essential for the proper implementation of the Orde r and stresses upon the Ministry 
to strengthen its enforcement mechanism to ensure t hat the objectives of the Order

inordinate delays in the framing of rules/regulatio ns after Acts are enforced.  The 
Ministries are not adhering to the time limit of si x months in this regard and also not 
taking Committee's approval in cases of delays beyo nd six months, as recommended by 
the Committee.  Besides, the Committee also found t hat despite repeated observations 
and recommendations by the Committee in its various  Reports, Ministries/Departments 
continue to lay their notifications, etc. on the Table of the House after considerable delays 
spanning from months to years.  Around 33% delayed notifications are laid with no delay 
statement explaining the reason for delay.  And eve n when such statements are attached, 
unacceptable excuses like delays in arranging print ed copies are being given.  The 
Committee felt that the Ministries/Departments are not taking its observations and 
recommendations seriously and have a casual attitud e towards framing and laying of 
these rules/regulations - an important duty towards  Parliament.  No senior officers, it 
appears, are monitoring this exercise in the Minist ries.  The Committee's concern 
centered mainly around the serious implications of delayed framing and laying of 
notification containing rules/regulations/orders, e tc.  The Committee is constrained to 
infer that Ministries/Departments may be doing so d eliberately with a view to evading 
Parliament's scrutiny of the rules/regulations that  are delegated by it to be framed by the 
Government.  Since such rules/regulations come into  force even before they are laid 
before Parliament, any delay in laying before Parli ament, in fact, prevents Members to 
exercise their right to get them modified/annulled by moving a Motion.  And this is what 
exactly happening today.  Another disturbing proble m was delayed response to the 
Committee's communications from the Ministries, and  not acknowledging its letters, etc. 
in time.  So many cases of scrutiny of rules/regulations are pending before the Committee 
mainly due to pending responses from them for many years.  They go on seeking 
extension on one pretext or the other.  This has be come a norm than exception.  It highly 
restricts the normal flow of Committee's work and then parliamentary scrutiny.

possible courses of action on this issue.  Since it  amounted actually bypassing Parliament

but also of the House and its members, which can be invoked in this case.  To begin with, 
however, it was decided that its Chairperson should  write to all the Ministers in this 
regard.  As per its earlier decision, the Committee  has already summoned Secretaries of 
some Ministries to explain about this state of affa irs and would be calling others for this 
purpose.  The Committee also decided to apprise the  Hon’ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha

2. While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee noted in some cases considerable time lag 
between issue  of notifications and their laying. T he annexed statement also indicates the period 
of delay in cases where notifications have not been  laid as per the schedule prescribed by the 
Committee. It also shows notifications not accompan ied by a statement indicating the reasons for 
the delay. 
 

The observations/recommendations of the Committee i n respect of the specific 
Ministries/Departments where delay in laying of Notifications has been noticed are as follows: -  
 
(i) Ministry of Civil Aviation 
 
 Ministry of Civil Aviation  have laid only two Not ifications (Sl. Nos. 6-7) on the Table of 
the House during the Session. There has been delay of 4 to 5 months in each case and no delay 
statement had been  attached with these Notifications. 
    
   The Committee notes with concern that Ministry of C ivil Aviation have not cared to 
append a delay statement with any of two notificati ons laid by them during winter session 
of Parliament in the year 2012. Thus the Ministry h ave flouted the Committee’s 
recommendation contained in its 135 
th  Report that a delay statement be invariably 
appended in case of delay while laying the notifications on the Table of the House.  
 
 
 
(ii) Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
 
 Ministry of Corporate Affairs have laid 15 Notific ations (Sl. Nos. 32 to 46).  Out of these 
3 Notifications have been delayed by 4 to 5 months.  Only one Notification (Sl. No. 41) has been 

attached with delay statement and other two Notifications (Sl. Nos. 39 - 40) did not have any. The 
Ministry has stated that the Notification could not  be laid in prescribed time  because the 
Notification being too bulky (465 pages) could not be printed by the Government Press before the 
Monsoon Session. The printed Notification was recei ved by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
only when the Monsoon Session of Parliament was already over. 
   
The Committee finds the reason given by the Ministr y of Corporate Affairs untrue. 
As stated  the notification was handed over to it b y the Government Press only after the 
monsoon Session which had started on 8.8.2012 and c ontinued upto 7.9.2012. The 
notification date is 7 th  August, 2012 and there was sufficient time for the Ministry to process 
the notification for laying. The Ministry was requi red to lay this notification during 
Monsoon Session itself there being more them 15 day s Session after it was notified. The 
Committee takes a serious note of this and directs the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to stick 
to procedure and schedule for the laying of notification in future. 
 
(iii)  Ministry of Defence 
 
The only Notification that the Ministry of Defence (Sl. No. 77) have laid is delayed by 8 
months with delay statement appended thereto. The reasons for delay given by the Ministry are as 
under:- 
 

“Recruitment Rules framed for the post of Additiona l Director General, in the Indian 
Coast Guard, Ministry of Defence were sent to the G overnment of India Press, Mayapuri for 
publication in the Official Gazette of India in Apr il, 2012. It took some time to get the published 
copies of Notification from the Government of India  Press. The sitting of the 11 th  Session of 15 th  
Lok Sabha and 226 th  Session of Rajya Sabha concluded on 07.09.2012. As  such the Recruitment 
rules could not be laid during aforesaid Session of Parliament, 2012. 
The delay in laying of papers on the Table of Lok S abha/Rajya Sabha is due to delay in 
getting published copies of the Recruitment Rules. It is requested that the marginal delay on the 
part of Ministry of Defence may kindly be condoned. 
 
The Committee finds the  reasons given by the Minis try of Defence for 8 months 
delay in laying of notification misleading. It was sent to Government Press in April, 2012  
and had it been properly tracked it would have been  laid during the Monsoon Session itself. 
Ministry did not give that dates when the printed c opies were received by it from the Press. 
As a result, it is not possible to apportion the re sponsibility. Ministry infact have tried to 
mislead the Committee and tried to lay the blame on  the Press. This is not acceptable to the 
Committee and it cautions the Ministry to be carefu l in future.  The Committee hopes that 
Ministry of Defence would take action accordingly i n order to comply with the prescribed 
schedule in the matter of laying of statutory Notifications . 
 
(iv) Ministry of Environment and Forests 

 
 Ministry of Environment and Forests have laid 6 Not ifications (Sl. Nos. 48 to 53) during 
the Session. Out of these, two Notifications (Sl. N o. 48 - 49) have been delayed by 6 months and 
no delay statement has been appended to both of them. 
  
 The Committee notes that two of its notifications which have not only been delayed 
by six months but also do not have any delay statem ent attached to them. The Committee 
views it seriously  reiterate its recommendations ( contained in its 135 
th  Report) that in case 
there is delay in laying of Statutory Orders, the c oncerned Ministry/Department should 
invariably append a delay statement. 
 
(v) Ministry of Finance 
 (Department of Financial Services) 
 
 Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Servi ces) have laid 30 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 71 to 100).  Out of these 19 Notifications (Sl . Nos. 76 – 94) have been delayed. The delay 
period ranges from 17 months to 27 months. All of t hese have been attached with delay 
statement. The reasons for delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
 “The Copies of the Gazettee Notifications could no t be laid on the Table of the Rajya 
Sabha as printed copies of the same were not receiv ed from Regional Rural Banks in time. The 

delay has occurred as the Regional Rural Banks whic h are spread out all over the country have to 
send the Regulations to Government Press, New Delhi  for publication. Thereafter, these are sent 
back to the concerned Regional Rural Banks which th en sent it to the Ministry. The delay is thus 
in the administrative procedure/process.” 
 
 The Committee does not accept the reasons of delay given by the Ministry of Finance 
(Department of Financial Services) and expresses it s serious concern over such inordinate 
delay which ranges from 17 months to 27 months. The  Committee wonders  that how can 
administrative procedural process take 17 to 27 mon ths to receive Notifications and 
complete procedural formalities. The Committee feel s that Ministry did not take adequate 
precaution to avoid the delay and made no serious e fforts to lay the Notifications in time 
which is in contravention of its statutory obligati on to Parliament. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry must take appropriate step to remove lacuna, if any 
administrative or any other causing such long delay  and wish it  would strive to keep delay 
to the minimum by playing a more proactive role and  pursuing concerned organisations to 
act with promptness in future.  
 
(vi) Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
 
 The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare have lai d 7 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 165 to 
171). Five of these Notifications  have been delaye d by 6 months. Out of 5 delayed Notifications 

2 notifications (Sl. Nos. 168-169) have been accomp anied with delay statement and other 3 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 165-167) have no delay statement appended to it. The reasons given by the 
Ministry are as follows:- 
 
  “……The aforesaid Notification before it could be laid on the Table of both Houses of 
Parliament  at earliest in monsoon session of Parli ament was challenged in the High Court of 
Bombay and High court of Delhi and some portion of the amendments has since been stayed by 
the Hon’ble High Courts. As the matter remained sub judice, the matter was referred to Ministry 
of Parliamentary Affairs for their advice whether under the circumstances it would be correct and 
appropriate to lay the Gazette Notification on the amendment of the Rules or it would be 
appropriate to wait till the disposal of the Court Cases. Soon after the receipt of the advice the 
process for laying the papers was initiated. 
 
 Now, the Notification G.S.R. 418 (E) is proposed t o be laid on the Table of both Houses of  
Parliament in the Winter Session of Parliament.” 
 
  “The Drugs and Cosmetics (4 
th  Amendment) Rules, 2012 under the Drugs and Cosmeti cs 
Act, 1940 were published in the Gazette of India, E xtraordinary, vide G.S.R. 575(E), dated 17 th  
July, 2012. Inadvertently, the notification could n ot be laid during the previous Monsoon Session 
of Parliament, 2012.” 
    

The Committee have noted the reason by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
that due to matter being subjudice, the notificatio n could not be laid in time. The reasons 
given by the Ministry seems to be justified and wel l taken. The Committee, however, are 
deeply anguished over the fact that delay in anothe r  case i.e. G.S.R. 575 (E) dated the 17 th  
July, 2012 was caused inadvertently by the Ministry . The Ministry should have been more 
vigilant to see that notification was laid within t he time schedule prescribed by the 
Committee. The Committee, therefore, impress upon t he Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare to be watchful so that such inadvertent delay is avoided in future. 
 
(vii) Ministry of Home Affairs  
  
The Ministry of Home Affairs have laid 22 Notificat ions (Sl. Nos. 174 - 195) during the 
Session. Out of total Notifications laid 15 (68.1%)  Notifications have been delayed by 3 months 
to  5 months and moreover no delay statement has been appended to any of them.  
 
The Committee expresses its unhappiness over the la rge proportion of Notifications 
which comes around 68.1% of total notifications bei ng delayed by the Ministry. The 
Committee further takes serious note of the fact th at the Ministry even did not bother to 
provide the reasons for such delayed laying of Noti fications. In absence of any delay 
statement with any of the delayed notifications Com mittee finds it difficult to ascertain 
causes of delay. The Committee invite attention to its recommendations made in 135 
th  

Report wherein it is laid down that it is essential  to append a delay statement in case of 
delay in laying of statutory orders. The committee,  therefore, impresses upon the Ministry 
of Home Affairs to strictly adhere to the time sche dule in laying of Notifications and should 
invariably append delay statement in each case of  delayed notifications .  
 
(viii)   Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas 
 
During the Session the Ministry of Petroleum and Na tural Gas have laid total 9 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 208 to 216) on the Table of  the House.  Out of these 4 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 210, 213 - 215) have been delayed by 3 months to 8 months whereas   no delay statement 
was attached to any of these Notifications. 
  
The Committee impress upon the Ministry of Petroleu m and Natural Gas  that it is 
their responsibility to ensure the timely laying of  notifications and take appropriate action 
in order to comply with the prescribed schedule for  laying and in case where there is delay, 
the statement explaining the reasons for such dealy  should invariable be accompanied with 
them. The Committee hopes that  the Ministry of Pet roleum and Natural Gas would avoid 
such delays and would append a delay statement in all such cases of delay in future.  
 
 
(ix) Ministry of  Power 

 
The Ministry of Power have laid 6 Notifications (Sl . Nos. 217 - 222) and out of which 2 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 221-222) have been delayed.  The delay period ranges from 8 months to 9 
months, both of them are accompanied by delay state ment. The reasons for delay given by the 
Ministry is as under:- 
  
“The notification for Accounting format of DVC was published on 30.03.2012 in the 
Gazette of India. 
 
The notification for the Rule 31 and Rule 25 of DVC  was published on 29 
th  February, 
2012 in the Gazette of India. 
 
The notification for rule 21 and Rule 25 of DVC wer e published in 28 
th  February, 2012 
and received in April, 2012, the notification for a ccounting format of DVC was published 
on 30.03.2012 in the Gazette of India but received in DVC Desk in May, 2012. 
 
Inadvertently due to exigency of the works the noti fications for the revised rules for 
Accounting format of DVC, Rule 31 and Rule 25 of DVC could not be laid on the table of 
the House during the Monsoon Session.” 
 

The Committee takes serious note of the fact that N otifications were delayed 
inadvertently due to exigency of work. This means t hat priority has been  accorded to other 
works and  the work of laying of notifications has been sidelined. The Committee therefore, 
impress upon the Ministry of Power to accord top priority to laying of notifications which is 
a statutory obligation. 
  
(x) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways have la id overall 25 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 223-247) and out of which 12 Notifications  ha ve been delayed by 4 months to 1 year. 
Eleven Notifications (Sl. Nos. 223 - 226, 228-230, 240-242 & 247) have no delay statement 
appended to them. Only one notification (Sl. No. 22 7) has delay statement appended to it. The 
reason of delay given by the Ministry is that it to ok some time to collect the papers and complete

The Committee does not accept the reasons of the de lay given by the Ministry of 
Road Transport and Highways that it took some time to collect the papers and complete the 
procedural formalities. The Committee wonders how c an it take one year to receive

view of the fact that even after delay of one year in certain case Ministry did not feel it 
necessary to append a delay statement so as to appr ise the Parliament of the reasons of 
delay in laying of Notifications on the Table of th e House. The Committee recommends that 
the Ministry should initiate urgent measures so as to avoid delay in completing the 
procedural formalities so that such delay can be eliminated.  
 
(xi) Ministry of Shipping 
 
The Ministry of Shipping have laid 3 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 248 - 250). Out of these 1 
Notification (Sl. No. 248) has been delayed by 2 ye ars and 1 month. There is no delay statement 
appended to it. 
 
The Committee are not happy that out of 3 Notificat ions that Ministry of shipping 
have laid, one Notification has been delayed by mor e than 2 years. Further there is no 
reason given for this inordinate delay.  This is in  contravention of Committee’s 
recommendation given in its 135 Report that Notific ation which are delayed should 
invariably be accompanied by delay statement. The C ommittee would like the Ministry of 
Shipping to take necessary steps to obviate such de lay and in case of delay in laying of 
Notifications, delay statement should invariably be accompanied with them. 
 
(xii) Ministry of Urban Development 

 
Ministry of Urban Development have laid 2 Notificat ions (Sl. Nos. 255-256) during the 
Session. Out of these, only one Notification (Sl. N o. 255) has been delayed by 9 months and no 
delay statement has been appended to it. 
 
The Committee takes a serious view not only about t he delay in laying one of its 
Notifications on the Table of the House but also fa ilure to append the delay statement with 
them. The Ministry/Department must know about the p ossible implications of failing to 
meet this requirement. It must ensure to append a d elay statement in all such cases in 
future .  
 
(xiii) Ministry of Women and Child Development 
 Ministry of Women and Child Development have laid 2 Notifications
 (Sl. Nos. 257 to 
258) out of which 1 Notification has been delayed ( Sl. No. 257) by 10 months and delay 
statement has been appended to it. The reason for delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
   
  “……The Recruitment Rules of various posts in NCPC R were published in the Gazette of 
India dated 08.02.2012, however, provisions under R Rs were being re-examined. As a result, 
copies of Gazette notification could not be laid on the table of both the Houses of Parliament. 

  The copies of Gazette notification as required un der Section 35(3) of CPCR Act are now 
being laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha.” 
 
  The Committee has noted the reply given by the Mini stry of Women and Child 
Development. The Committee would like the Ministry of Women and Child Development to 
lay all the Notifications as per schedule given in the recommendation of Committee in its 
131 
st  Report. 
 
3.   Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/De partments to take immediate steps to 
ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate legi slation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes 
to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Department s of the Government of India, particularly, the 
defaulting ones, the following recommendations, as contained in its 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 152 
nd  ,   192 nd  
and 201st  Reports: 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d be laid (i) if the House is not in 
Session, during the Session immediately following t he date of publication of the Order in 
the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Se ssion, on the date of the publication of the 
Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between the date of publication and 
the date of the closing of the Session is less than  15 clear days, before the expiry of the 
Session immediately following the said Session. All  the Ministries/Departments of 

Government of India should henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of 
the Orders issued under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 December 2000) 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized tha t it is essential that in case there is 
a delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the conc erned Ministry/Department should 
invariably append a delay statement along with the notifications being laid so as to apprise 
Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee de sires all Ministries/Departments to 
take a note of this, since the intension is that th rough the process of formulation of a delay 
statement the Ministry is able to introspect, ident ify bottlenecks and devise remedial 
measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 July 2001) 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on should be assigned a distinctive 
number in order to give it a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to ex ercise caution in this regard. In case 
where there are more than one notification under a single file, the Ministries/Departments 

should ensure that the file number on each notifica tion should be suitably distinguished 
from one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the Commi ttee over delay in laying of 
Notifications on the Table of the House, the Committee also express their deep concern over 
delay in framing of rules/regulations under differe nt Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report 
presented to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended  that the rule-making process should 
be completed within a period of six months of the c oming into force on an Act. The 
committee has further recommended that in case a Mi nistry is not able to adhere to this 
time limit, it should seek extension of time for co mpleting the rule-making process. The 
recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 
 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-making process c ould well have been 
completed within the time limit of six months which  the Committee has laid down for 
making of rules under an Act after coming into forc e of that Act. Where however, a 
Ministry does not find it possible to adhere to the  time limit, they should inform the 
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make rules  within the time limit and seek 
extension of time for completing the rule-making process.” 

 
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the f act that the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India are n ot complying with the Committee’s 
recommendation to complete the process of framing of subordinate legislation contemplated 
under various Acts of Parliament within a period of  six months. At the same time, the 
Committee also does not receive requests for extens ion of time for completing the rule-
making process in terms of its recommendations as a bove from most of the 
Ministries/Departments. The committee takes a serio us note of the prevailing situation in 
which the Ministries/Departments are neither able t o complete the task of framing 
rules/regulations under different Acts within the g iven six months’ period nor do they suo-
motu  approach the Committee for seeking extension of ti me. The Committee further notes 
that in order to ensure timely framing of rules/reg ulations it has taken an initiative to 
monitor the progress of framing of subordinate legi slation in respect of all legislations 
brought about by different Ministries/Departments o f Government of India from the year 
2003 onwards with a view to ensure that the framing  of subordinate legislation is not 
delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the res ponses from the 
Ministries/Departments have not been prompt in this  monitoring exercise undertaken on 
behalf of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once again reiterates its 
recommendation that the Ministries/Departments shou ld ensure putting in place 

subordinate legislation positively within a period of six months of coming into force of the 
Act. The Committee further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet with this 
deadline, they should invariably approach the Committee for seeking extension of time. The 
Committee further recommends that in cases where th e time limit of six months is not 
adhered to, they should, while laying rules/regulat ions before the Parliament invariably lay 
a statement explaining the reasons why the framing of rules/regulations was delayed beyond 
six months so as to keep the Parliament apprised of  the compliance of the Parliament’s 
mandate  conferred upon the Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2011)

Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are published in the of ficial Gazette before being laid on the 
Table of the House. Even after they are laid, it is  ver difficult to get access to these 
notifications. The Committee recommends that such R ules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on 
the Table of the House should be invariably uploade d on the websites of respective 
Ministries immediately on the same day when they ha ve been laid on the Table of the 
House, for information of Members of Parliament and people at large for their easy access.

2.  The Chairperson welcomed the Members of the Com mittee and thereafter the 
Committee took up the following draft Reports for consideration one-by-one. 
 
(i) Two Hundred and Fourth Report on the Statutory Orde rs laid on the Table of the 
Rajya Sabha during the 227 
th  Session. 
 
(ii) Two Hundred and Fifth Report on the Regional Rural Banks (Appointment and 
Promotion of Officers and Employees) Rules, 2010;  
 
(iii) Two Hundred and Sixth Report on the Gas Cylinder Rules, 2004; and 
 
(iv) Two Hundred and Seventh Report on Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation 
of Supply and Distribution and Prevention of Malpra ctices) Order, 2005 and the 
Electrical Wires, Cables, Appliances and Protection Devices and Accessories (Quality 
Control) Order, 2003. 
 
3.  The Committee adopted these Reports with some a mendments suggested by the 
Members.   

 
4.  The Committee while discussing the draft Two Hu ndred and Fourth Report on the 
Statutory Orders laid on the Table of the Rajya Sab ha during the 227 
th  Session was of the 
opinion that its repeated recommendation for timely  laying of the subordinate legislation 
framed under different Acts before the House, have not evoked the desired promptness in the 
Ministries/Departments. However, the Committee has noted some improvement in this 
regard. While 33.5% notifications were delayed duri ng 226 th  Session, it came down to 
26.25% during 227 th  Session. It was, therefore, decided to continue th e exercise of 
summoning the Secretaries of the concerned Ministri es before the Committee to explain such 
delays.  
 
5.  While discussing the reasons of delay in laying  of notifications by 
Ministries/Departments the Committee noticed that i n most of the cases reasons 
citied/forwarded by the Ministry/Department has bee n the late receipt of printed copies of 
notifications from Government of India Press. To un derstand the problem and for its solution 
the Committee decided to summon the Secretary, Mini stry of Urban Development and 
administrative Ministry of Government of India Pres s responsible for printing Government of 
India Notifications. 
  

6.  The Committee authorized its Chairperson and in  her absence Shri Vijay 
Jawaharlal Darda and in his absence Dr. K.P. Ramali ngam to present the Reports to the 
House on 03 rd  December, 2013. 
 
 7.  The Chairperson thanked the Members present an d meeting was concluded at 2.40
